question: Can a soft elapsed-time temporal relevance term ever outperform (or complement) hard version/validity-interval filtering on amended regulatory texts, or does the hard constraint dominate it?
description: Prior et al. (arxiv:2605.23497) report that temporal validity must be enforced as a hard constraint and that 'what is retrieved (the correct timeframe) matters more than how it is retrieved'. TempRALM's soft elapsed-time decay is monotone toward the nearest/newest version, with no notion of in-force intervals, and Prior et al. document recency bias as a failure mode. If hard interval filtering dominates, the soft temporal term may add nothing or actively harm historically anchored queries.
rationale: Determines whether the proposed soft temporal component has any value over the simpler, already-demonstrated hard filter; this is the central empirical question after the novelty finding.
